messages:
marc: Heads-up — we've been seeing p99 token-latency spikes (~2–3s) across many inference hosts in eastus2 since ~07:10 UTC. Mostly GPU nodes. Anyone oncall?
anya: I'm on it, getting pages. p99 for text-gen route jumped from ~180ms -> ~2.1s, throughput steady. Taking a couple hosts OOS to investigate.
kai: I pushed a change this morning to tighten egress burst policies for the gpufarm DS: <https://git.company/repo/pulls/3245|PR#3245>. Scoped to kube-node-egress class, but it did touch the host shaper bootstrap. 0/5 canary looked fine.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started: host-traffic-policy v2 -> eastus2-gpufarm (42 hosts) by kai — sha: b3f2a9c
devops: Quick checks — run this on a repro host:
```
# tc qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: root refcnt 2 limit 10240 ecn
qdisc tbf 1: parent 0:1 rate 9600Mbit burst 64Kb latency 50ms
qdisc ingress ffff: parent ffff:fff1 ???
```
Looks like tbf is present AND there's a police on the bond0. That combination can cause uneven per-flow queuing.
eli: I grabbed `tc filter show` and found a clsact -> police rule applied host-wide by the daemonset label matcher. Sample: `police rate 9600mbit burst 160kmtu conform-exceed drop`. Also saw BPF mirror rules for telemetry. Ran iperf3 between two GPU hosts: throughput saw microbursts and packet loss spikes.
marc: RDMA checks show ib_read_lat 99th jumped as well, so east-west fabric affected, not just TCP queuing.
anya: rolling back the host-traffic-policy on 3 hot hosts fixed p99 immediately (confirmed by dashboard). Reverting rollout now for the rest. :thumbsup:
kai: ugh, my DS label selector accidentally matched host-pool=gpufarm and host=all (bad templating). I'll open a revert and a stricter selector. Plan: revert -> test on 3 hosts -> staged 10% -> full.
sre-oncall: INC-4872 created for the availability regression, timeline + affected tenants attached. Adding tags: qos-misapply, eastus2, gpufarm.
devops: Proposed guardrail: daemonset rollout needs node-label gating + dry-run mode that only prints tc commands before apply. Also add a healthcheck that rejects changes if p99 increases >20% during canary.
eli: note for postmortem — interaction between tbf + police + sysctl net.core.rmem defaults caused bufferbloat under bursts. We'll collect `tc -s qdisc` outputs and ifstat/ib stats.
marc: thanks all. Kai — please ping when revert PR is up. We'll assign PM/SE for follow-up to add rollout guardrails.
kai: PR opened: <https://git.company/repo/pulls/3250|revert host-traffic-policy>, will coordinate the staged reapply with a tighter selector and canary checks. Sorry folks. :facepalm:
anya: monitoring note: set temp alert to page at p99 > 500ms for text-gen on eastus2 until postmortem done.
marc: closing thread — recorded notes in INC-4872. Postmortem requested by EOD.
